# Markov augmentation and stationary memory law {#sec-mifs}

## The frozen augmented kernel

Fix $\theta$. Let $\mathsf Y=\mathbb{R}^d\times[0,\infty)^d$ be the memory space, with its Euclidean product norm, and let $\mathsf Z=\mathsf X\times\mathsf Y$ carry the product sigma-algebra. Define

$$
T_\theta(x',m,v)=
\begin{pmatrix}
\alpha m+(1-\alpha)H_\theta(x')\\
\beta v+(1-\beta)H_\theta(x')^{\odot2}
\end{pmatrix}.
$$ {#eq-memory-map}

For $u=(m,v)$, also write $T_\theta(x,u)=T_\theta(x,m,v)$. For the frozen recursions, $Z_n=(X_n,M_n,V_n)$ has transition kernel

$$
Q_\theta((x,u),dx'\,du')
=P_\theta(x,dx')\,\delta_{T_\theta(x',u)}(du').
$$ {#eq-augmented-kernel}

Conditional on the current state, the next observation has law $P_\theta(x,\cdot)$ and the next memory is a deterministic measurable function of that observation and the current memory. Hence $Z_n$ is Markov. For two memory states driven by the same observation,

$$
\begin{aligned}
\|T_\theta(x',m,v)-T_\theta(x',\widetilde m,\widetilde v)\|^2
&=\alpha^2\|m-\widetilde m\|^2+\beta^2\|v-\widetilde v\|^2\\
&\leq\kappa^2\|(m,v)-(\widetilde m,\widetilde v)\|^2,
\qquad \kappa=\max\{\alpha,\beta\}<1.
\end{aligned}
$$ {#eq-same-driver-memory-contraction}

This contracts the memory coordinates along a common driving path. It is not a contraction assertion for $Q_\theta$ on the full augmented space: different initial driving states have not been coupled.

## Identification of the stationary memories

::: {#cor-stationary-memory-law}
## Stationary memory representation

Under @asm-frozen-driver, $Q_\theta$ has a unique invariant probability $\nu_\theta$. Its driving marginal is $\pi_\theta$ and

$$
\nu_\theta=
\operatorname{Law}_{\mathbb{P}_\theta^{\mathrm{stat}}}
(X_0^\theta,M^\theta,V^\theta),
$$ {#eq-stationary-joint-law}

where $M^\theta,V^\theta$ are the stationary histories in @eq-stationary-memories. Consequently,

$$
F(\theta)=\int_{\mathsf Z}
\frac{m}{\sqrt v+\varepsilon}\,
\nu_\theta(dx\,dm\,dv).
$$ {#eq-stationary-adam-integral}
:::

::: {.proof}
Define $M_k^\theta$ and $V_k^\theta$ by shifting the infinite series in @eq-stationary-memories to time $k$. Their almost-sure convergence follows from @lem-stationary-memories and stationarity. They satisfy the frozen recursions, while the joint process $(X_k^\theta,M_k^\theta,V_k^\theta)_{k\in\mathbb{Z}}$ is stationary. Its one-time law is therefore invariant for @eq-augmented-kernel.

For uniqueness, let $\eta$ be another invariant probability of $Q_\theta$. Its driving marginal must equal $\pi_\theta$, by the uniqueness assumed in @asm-frozen-driver. Couple initial states with laws $\eta$ and $\nu_\theta$ so that their driving coordinates agree, and then use the same driving transitions for both memory recursions. Their memory difference after $n$ steps is bounded by $\kappa^n\|U_0-\widetilde U_0\|$. This tends to zero almost surely without a moment assumption on the two initial memories. For every bounded measurable test function that is uniformly Lipschitz in the memory coordinate, bounded convergence gives equality of the two stationary expectations. Such tests determine probability measures on $\mathsf X\times\mathsf Y$, hence $\eta=\nu_\theta$. The integral representation follows from @lem-stationary-memories and $\varepsilon>0$.
:::

This stationary identification does not require a geometric contraction estimate for the driving chain. Such an estimate is introduced in the next section to control distances between augmented transition laws from different initial driving states, and subsequently to compare kernels with different frozen parameters.
